findings.problem: Increment A requires a decision record to be drafted, accepted at an owner checkpoint, then implemented, but its Evidence permits “one or two local commits.” Project policy and the plans contract require exactly one verified, reviewed local commit per increment, so this increment cannot be executed as written.
findings.suggestion: Split the decision and its implementation into separate increments (for example A and A-A), each with its own verification, review, evidence, and single commit; update downstream dependencies accordingly.

findings.location: docs/plans/2026-11-03-module-conformance-levels-and-hooks.md: Assumptions and constraints, “Increments A, B and C are separable”
findings.problem: The claim that any of A, B, or C may be dropped conflicts with the declared dependency chain B → A and C → B. Dropping A necessarily prevents B and C, and dropping B prevents C.
findings.suggestion: State that only dependency-closed portions may be omitted, or revise the increments and dependencies to make the intended optionality real.

summary: The plan has an increment/commit-unit violation that must be resolved before it can be relied on.
